topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Probability

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability
sections.content: Briefly revisit the idea of 'updating' information. Define P(A|B) as the probability of A given that B has occurred, visualized as zooming into a subset of a Venn diagram.
sections.example: A bowl has 5 red apples and 5 green pears. If you pick a fruit and it is red, the 'universe' of possibilities shrinks from 10 to just the 5 red fruits.

sections.title: Defining Independence
sections.content: Introduce independence: Two events are independent if the occurrence of one doesn't change the probability of the other. Visually, P(A|B) = P(A).
sections.example: Flipping a coin (Event A) and rolling a die (Event B). No matter what the coin shows, the die remains equally likely to land on any side.

sections.title: The Core: Bayes' Theorem
sections.content: Introduce the theorem as a bridge between 'what we know' (prior) and 'new evidence' (likelihood). Use a formula graphic where terms are color-coded: P(H|E) = [P(E|H) * P(H)] / P(E).
sections.example: A medical test (Evidence) for a rare disease (Hypothesis). Even if the test is 99% accurate, the low prevalence (Prior) changes the interpretation of a positive result.

sections.title: Application: The Detective Robot
sections.content: Apply the theorem to a dynamic scenario. Show how a robot updates its 'belief' about its location after receiving sensor data. Link the concept of 'updating' back to the previous sections.
sections.example: A robot senses a wall. Using Bayes' Theorem, it combines its previous location estimate (Prior) with the sensor reading (Evidence) to calculate a new, more accurate position (Posterior).

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Summary slide: Independence means information is irrelevant; Bayes' Theorem means information is transformative. A final visual summary comparing the two.
sections.example: Independence = Parallel paths; Bayes' = A feedback loop that refines our understanding of the world.
